purpose: Teach Trader Apprentice to identify short candidates after capitulation instead of only waiting for long reclaims.
source: K1m6a/Coinwise-style screenshots from the live case sequence

observed_sequence.interpretation: Massive forced-long flush. Do not short the liquidation low blindly and do not call a bottom from liquidation size alone.

Aggressive buying and OI both rebuilt strongly, but price response was weak and remained far below dVAL. This is buyer effort plus rapid re-leveraging below broken value: a fragile bounce, not confirmed recovery.

root_cause: The existing Trader Apprentice logic was asymmetric: bearish observations mostly disabled longs or returned RISK_OFF, but did not promote a separate SHORT_CANDIDATE workflow.
The system over-focused on waiting for a long reclaim after the flush and underweighted failure-to-reclaim as an actionable directional signal.
The model needed an efficiency test: large CVD recovery + large OI rebuild that produces only a small price bounce below dVAL is evidence of buyer inefficiency / passive seller control.
The model needed path-aware crowding logic: rapid post-capitulation OI rebuild below broken value can create a fresh liquidation layer if price cannot reclaim structure.

preconditions: A large long-liquidation flush has already occurred.
Price remains below broken value / dVAL.
OI rebuilds rapidly after the flush.
CVD improves or buyers become aggressive, but price response is weak relative to that effort.
ideal_short_setup.trigger: Bounce into the first broken structural level (preferably dVAL / prior-day-low cluster) then rejection or failure to accept above it.
confirmation: Price rolls over from the failed reclaim.
CVD stops recovering or turns down.
OI remains elevated/rises as price weakens, OR OI begins flushing only after the rejection has already confirmed the trap.
A lower high or failed retest forms below dVAL/dPOC.
avoid: Do not initiate the first short at the capitulation low after a vertical liquidation candle.
Do not short solely because OI rose; OI does not identify side by itself.
Do not short a successful dVAL/dPOC reclaim with Price UP + CVD UP + OI UP.
ideal_short_setup.invalidation: Acceptance back above dVAL and especially dPOC with positive price response to CVD and non-pathological OI growth.
ideal_short_setup.continuation_trigger: A fresh low after failed reclaim is higher quality if CVD is down and OI is flat/up; if OI is collapsing violently, treat it as continuation deleveraging and avoid chasing too late.

efficiency_features_for_model.failed_reclaim_score: higher when price remains below dVAL/dPOC despite positive CVD and rising OI
efficiency_features_for_model.crowding_warning: OI rebuild after capitulation is dangerous when price cannot reclaim value
efficiency_features_for_model.path_priority: Use intrawindow high/low, reclaim attempts and OI path; endpoint-only matrices can miss traps.

decision_rule.if: post-capitulation bounce + CVD UP + OI UP + price remains below dVAL and shows weak response
decision_rule.then: classify as FRAGILE_RELEVERAGING_BELOW_VALUE and arm SHORT_CANDIDATE_ON_FAILED_RECLAIM
decision_rule.preferred_execution_logic: wait for retest/rejection of broken value or a confirmed rollover; short the failed repair, not the liquidation low

lesson: The missed short was not predictable from one bearish candle; it became predictable when the post-flush bounce showed strong buyer effort and strong OI rebuild without structural reclaim. The actionable information was failure of recovery efficiency. Trader Apprentice must be symmetric: long reclaims and short failed-reclaims are mirror-image opportunities.
